arxiv-2605-08853: Big models are often treated as black boxes, but Sohan Venkatesh argues the answers lie in architecture, not scale. arxiv-2605-09253: Distilling a big model into a small one on-policy produces rock tokens — stubborn tokens that resist the transfer. arxiv-2605-09353: Spies do not just encrypt — they hide the fact that they are communicating at all. arxiv-2605-09553: Surfaces meeting a vector field at a prescribed angle generalize constant-angle surfaces; torse-forming fields give them structure. Muhittin Evren Aydin, Esra Dilmen, and Büşra Karakaya study them in Riemannian manifolds. The 2026 paper is differential geometry on angled surfaces.

plos-pone-0003453: Biotechnologists turned cows into drug factories in this 2008 cloning paper. plos-pone-0003553: Plant biologists built a mathematical engine for eternal youth in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003653: In 2008, a team asked what caps human sports records. Studying ten famed outdoor races from Oxford to Hawaii, they found the body's own limits setting the ceiling, not will or training. The work maps the bodily walls that even the greatest athletes cannot climb past.
plos-pone-0003753: In 2008, Zhang, Qiu, and Hu linked a pregnancy vitamin to diabetes risk. Mothers with low blood vitamin D faced higher odds of gestational diabetes. The finding adds a nutritional thread to the story of blood-sugar trouble in pregnancy.
plos-pone-0003853: In 2008, a team studied life in a river of acid. The red river's ecology reconciles competing ideas about who lives where and why.
plos-pone-0003953: In 2008, Schillaci, Waitzkin, and Sharmen traced how Medicaid churn hit kids' shots. Changing enrollments in New Mexico rippled into the state's immunization program. The analysis shows bureaucratic turnover translating into missed vaccines for poor children.
plos-pone-0004053: In 2008, Feng, Reeves, and Lan reset the clock on cholera's pandemics. Their recalibrated molecular clock dated the pandemic Vibrio cholerae clones independently. plos-pone-0004153: In 2009, Holmes, James, and Coode-Bate proposed Tetris as trauma first aid. Playing the computer game after trauma might cut flashback build-up. The visuospatial game could compete with intrusive images for mind space. The cognitive proposal offers a cheap early intervention.
plos-pone-0004253: In 2009, Paupe, Dassa, and Goncalves found a defense failing in sick neurons. Impaired Nrf2 movement to the nucleus weakened the oxidative stress response. plos-pone-0004353: In 2009, Petit and Nicolas watched skin's first blueprint unfold. Large-scale clonal analysis revealed unexpected complexity in surface ectoderm shaping. plos-pone-0353753: Catching gut cancers early means simpler treatment and better odds. The diagnostic model outperformed single markers, offering clinics a cheap blood-based early warning.
plos-pone-0358253: A failing bearing can halt a whole factory. This paper built a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method on a dual-attention multi-scale convolutional network that reads vibration signals. The attention mechanism focuses the network on the fault’s signature frequencies, catching failures earlier and more reliably.
plos-pone-0336553: Paying employees to quit smoking works — but building the program takes planning. The step-by-step strategy shows employers how to turn research evidence into a program that actually sticks.
plos-pone-0358353: Liver failure clouds the brain subtly — before standard tests catch it. This study showed eye movement analysis detects early neurological alterations in cirrhotic patients classified as not having minimal hepatic encephalopathy. plos-pone-0355953: Predicting which early AMD cases will progress to blinding late disease could save sight. The PRIME study protocol outlines predicting progression risk in the aging eye through imaging and multimodal evaluation. The planned study aims to catch converters early — when intervention still helps.
plos-pone-0357153: Predicting ultra-high-performance concrete’s compressive strength saves costly lab testing. This paper compared machine learning models for the task head-to-head. The bake-off identifies which algorithms engineers can actually trust with their mix designs.
plos-pone-0354453: Among the Bahnar people of Vietnam’s Central Highlands, forests are alive with spirits — and that shapes everything. plos-pone-0356253: Vaccinating children in Ethiopia’s urban slums and pastoralist regions faces unique obstacles. The grounded findings give immunization programs a realistic playbook for hard-to-reach communities.
plos-pone-0355853: Calcium binding sites control protein function — and predicting them accelerates biology. The algorithm pinpoints where calcium docks — illuminating signaling pathways across all of life.
plos-pone-0352253: Carbapenem-resistant gut bacteria don’t distribute evenly — they track environmental injustice. The findings link antibiotic resistance to the same disadvantaged neighborhoods that bear pollution’s burden.
plos-pone-0355053: Selecting the best blastocyst for IVF — by AI segmentation — could improve success rates. plos-pone-0353353: The ‘white replacement’ narrative — a conspiracy theory with deadly consequences — spreads through elite discourse and public attention. This paper examined how those forces drive extremist mobilization. The analysis traces the pipeline from respectable rhetoric to violent action — essential for understanding and countering radicalization.
plos-pone-0354953: Digital productivity — ‘new quality productive forces’ — is pitched as China’s path to common prosperity. This paper researched the logical mechanism and path of that enablement. plos-pone-0354353: Stroke patients’ long-term care and outcomes in England vary by ethnicity — unjustly. This paper documented those ethnic disparities. The findings demand that stroke services confront the structural inequities shaping who recovers and who doesn’t.
europmc-pmc2794253: Plant biologists often need protoplasts, plant cells stripped of their walls, and this 2009 paper offers a simpler way to get them from Arabidopsis leaves. europmc-pmc2798753: Some strains of Staphylococcus aureus make a toxin called Panton-Valentine leukocidin that destroys white blood cells. europmc-pmc2829053: The inflammatory signal IL-1beta must be cut to become active, and this 2010 review looks beyond the usual suspects. europmc-pmc2873753: Hand, foot and mouth disease swept Singapore's children, and this 2003 paper traces the culprit. europmc-pmc2913853: The body's alarm can be turned down. This 2010 review looks at cooling inflammation by tuning TLR signals, the sensors that spot harm. The authors survey danger-signal paths as drug targets. Their overview points to calmer immune replies in disease.
europmc-pmc2914753: A second malaria parasite, Plasmodium vivax, threatens billions yet gets less attention. europmc-pmc2923753: Fungi armor themselves with chitin, and this 2010 review ties that armor to disease. The authors cover chitin synthesis and fungal pathogenesis in major pathogens. europmc-pmc2950153: Fatal Ebola wrecks the immune system from within. This 2010 paper finds human fatal Zaire Ebola infection pairs aberrant innate immunity with massive lymphocyte death. europmc-pmc3012653: Tiny-particle safety tests need true dosing. This 2010 paper brings ISDD, a model of how particles settle onto cells in lab dishes. The authors' math fixes the dose. Their tool improved nanosafety calls. Old tests overdosed cells without knowing it.
europmc-pmc3035253: Germ species got a digital yardstick. This 2010 paper defines bacterial species by comparing whole genomes on the computer. The authors' method replaces fussy lab hybridization. europmc-pmc3037053: Antimony poisons quietly. This 2010 review covers the toxic metal's harms to workers and patients. The authors survey poisoning cases. Their overview informs safety limits. europmc-pmc3057953: More sequences don't always crack hard trees. This 2011 paper explains why piling on DNA fails for the toughest family-tree puzzles. The authors diagnose the trap. europmc-pmc3063653: Flu needs animal stand-ins, and this 2010 review surveys them. The authors cover ferrets, mice, and more for flu disease and spread. Their overview guides virology. europmc-pmc3093253: Seaweed sugars carry healing power. This 2011 review maps the structures and health effects of sulfated sugars from sea algae. The authors survey the compounds. europmc-pmc6602353: The embryonic spinal cord builds itself through exquisitely timed gene activity - different genes switching on in different places at different moments. europmc-pmc6681553: Frailty - the slow slide into vulnerability - strikes many older adults, but how many newly each year? europmc-pmc6683253: Fish-oil capsules promise mood lifts - but does the science hold? Pooling dozens of rigorous trials, this meta-analysis measured omega-3s against depression, zooming in on EPA and DHA. The verdict: modest but real benefit, strongest in clinical depression.

gao-gaoreports-gao-07-653: Taxpayer-funded science was going dark in 2007 — GAO's report says the rules for sharing federal research needed clarifying. The findings press selected agencies to open up. The report's creed: the public paid for the discoveries, so the public should get to read them.
